headline: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026

Union Minister of Communications Hails India As The Data Capital Of The World

Broadband access grew from 6 crore to 103 crore in a decade, a 16x jump: Shri Scindia

Rolled out in 2022, India's 5G now covers 99.9% districts and 85% population in 26 months, with capex of Rs 4.5 lakh crore: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia

Smartphones are the new ‘bank branch’ for Indians: Union Minister of Communications

10 SEP 2026 10:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, called for an inclusive and trusted digital financial ecosystem, emphasising that before finance becomes intelligent, it must become inclusive. Speaking at the Global Fintech Festival 2026 in Mumbai, he said the telecom network, an invisible highway that cannot be seen, is the very foundation on which fintech evolves. Together with compute and trust, connectivity forms the new digital trinity powering the next phase of digital finance.

Highlighting the scale of India’s digital transformation, Shri Scindia said that around 25 crore people had access to the internet a decade ago, compared to 100 crore today. Broadband access has grown from just 6 crore to 103 crore, representing nearly 16 times growth in 10 years. He emphasised that technology must become ubiquitous, across India and the world.

The Union Minister said that smartphones have become bank branches, taking citizens from internet connectivity to credit and investment. With around 6.5 lakh villages becoming participants in the digital economy, he said every connected village can become a member of the global fintech ecosystem.

Highlighting India’s rapid 5G expansion, Shri Scindia said that following the launch of 5G in 2022, India achieved capability across 99.9% of districts, covering almost 85% of the population, within 26 months. Shri Scindia also noted that the rollout has been supported by over 5 lakh 5G base stations.

Furthermore, the Union Minister highlighted the sharp reduction in the cost of communications, noting that data costs have fallen to around 10 cents per GB. He said India has become the world’s cheapest data capital, making digital technology increasingly accessible.

Shri Scindia highlighted the journey of UPI, which began with around 90,000 transactions in its first month and has today scaled to more than 740 banks. UPI has processed around 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025–26, worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, demonstrating the scale that India’s Digital Public Infrastructure can achieve.

The Union Minister of Communications noted that 84% of domestic digital transactions take place on UPI, while India accounts for approximately 49% of the world’s real-time digital payment volumes. He credited the fintech ecosystem for this achievement and said that India’s success demonstrates the power of technology built at scale.

Union Minister Shri Scindia highlighted the success of UPI as an expression of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. He said the technology is being taken to nine countries at no cost to them, while the world is looking towards taking this model to the next 20 countries.

Additionally, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said the architecture of digital finance rests on networks that carry connections, trust and interoperable platforms that connect institutions. He underlined three principles: innovation scales when infrastructure is open; inclusion scales when infrastructure is affordable; and trust scales when infrastructure is secure.

Highlighting the role of Jan Dhan accounts and DigiLocker, the Union Minister said around 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts and 9 billion documents on DigiLocker have dramatically reduced the distance between citizens and their ability to access finance. He emphasised that finance no longer needs to depend on the physical presence of a bank branch. “The smartphone is the bank branch,” he said, noting that a smartphone can take fintech to every citizen.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia highlighted that fintech connectivity has reached almost every village in the North Eastern Region, driven by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s impetus and sankalp. Through Digital Bharat Nidhi, around 22,000 towers are being established across 34,000 villages without telecom connectivity, with the objective of ensuring 100% saturation.

Shri Scindia said that as India works towards 100% saturation on the mobile front, a new arterial system is being established, extending from mobile to terrestrial networks. He highlighted the role of Gram Panchayats in creating first-mile, middle-mile and last-mile connectivity to reach the remaining villages.

The Union Minister also highlighted the national AI capabilities and compute power converge with digital infrastructure, AI can personalise financial advice and credit and increasingly make financial services autonomous.

Shri Scindia emphasised that with greater intelligence comes greater responsibility. He called for financial systems to be ring-fenced, with strong firewalls and safeguards to protect citizens and their financial security.

Sanchar Saathi, a Government of India initiative that protects citizens against suspicious connections and enables stolen devices to be blocked. Shri Scindia highlighted the AI powered tool- ASTR, which has helped disconnect more than 88 lakh suspicious mobile connections.

The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator ring-fences suspicious transactions and helps stop fraudulent payments before money leaves citizens’ accounts. He called for SOPs across banking networks to strengthen the protection of citizens and their financial capabilities.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia emphasised the need to shift from detecting fraud after it happens to preventing it before it occurs. He said the objective must be to move from reactive security to predictive trust.

The Union Minister called for the creation of a Trust Grid for finance, bringing together telecom, digital identity, UPI and financial systems. He said greater convergence of Aadhaar and UPI can give every citizen the capability to participate in and benefit from the digital economy.

Shri Scindia said that if Digital India democratised access, Intelligent India must democratise intelligence. AI cannot remain the preserve of corporates or banks. It must become a tool available to every citizen, enabling each person to benefit from the transformation underway.

The Union Minister highlighted India’s indigenous 4G telecom stack, noting that telecom stacks have historically been developed by a small number of countries and companies. India has now produced its own domestic 4G stack and is working on 5G.

Shri Scindia said India’s 6G mission has already started, with the ambition of contributing 10% of global 6G patents and becoming a valuable partner in the development of 6G standards.

Concluding, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said India must “Innovate in India, serve in India, serve the world and serve it securely.” He said the ambition must be to move from a connected India to intelligent digital finance and then to empowered finance, and from Digital Public Infrastructure to trusted infrastructure.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
At the Global Fintech Festival 2026 in Mumbai on September 10, 2026, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia called for an inclusive, trusted, and intelligent digital financial ecosystem built on connectivity, compute, and security. He said smartphones are increasingly serving as “bank branches” and highlighted India’s rapid digital infrastructure and fintech growth.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Internet access increased from around 25 crore people a decade ago to 100 crore today, while broadband access rose from 6 crore to 103 crore—nearly 16 times growth.
- India’s 5G service, launched in 2022, reached 99.9% of districts and approximately 85% of the population within 26 months, supported by over 5 lakh base stations and ₹4.5 lakh crore in capital expenditure.
- Data costs have fallen to around 10 cents per GB, which Scindia described as making India the world’s cheapest data capital.
- Around 6.5 lakh villages are participating in the digital economy. In the North Eastern Region, Digital Bharat Nidhi is establishing about 22,000 towers across 34,000 villages to achieve 100% mobile-network saturation.
- UPI began with around 90,000 transactions in its first month and now operates across more than 740 banks.
- UPI processed approximately 24,162 crore transactions worth ₹314 lakh crore in FY 2025–26; it accounts for 84% of domestic digital transactions, while India represents approximately 49% of global real-time digital payment volumes.
- India is providing its UPI technology to nine countries at no cost, with the goal of extending the model to the next 20 countries.
- Around 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts and 9 billion documents stored through DigiLocker have expanded citizens’ access to financial services without requiring physical bank branches.
- Scindia identified three principles for digital finance: innovation scales through open infrastructure, inclusion through affordable infrastructure, and trust through secure infrastructure.
- He said AI can personalize financial advice and credit services, but called for ring-fenced systems, firewalls, safeguards, and standardized operating procedures to shift fraud protection from reactive detection to prevention.
- Sanchar Saathi and the AI-powered ASTR tool have helped disconnect more than 88 lakh suspicious mobile connections.
- The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator is intended to identify suspicious transactions and prevent fraudulent payments before funds leave citizens’ accounts.
- Scindia proposed a “Trust Grid for finance” integrating telecom networks, digital identity, UPI, and financial systems, with greater convergence of Aadhaar and UPI.
- He called for AI-enabled financial capabilities to be accessible to every citizen rather than limited to corporations or banks.
- The minister also highlighted India’s indigenous 4G telecom stack.

headline: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0

Central Sector Scheme approved with an outlay of ₹565.50 Crore for 2026–2031 to establish an integrated, GIS-based ‘Land Stack’

Sub-Registrar Offices to be upgraded into modern ‘Registration Seva Kendras’ modeled after Passport Seva Kendras

Every land parcel to receive a 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) alongside full georeferencing of cadastral maps

“Land is not merely property; it represents the pride of farmers and our generational heritage”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

10 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, formally launched the Operational Guidelines for the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 during a hybrid event held at Krishi Bhawan today. The launch brought together State Revenue and Registration Ministers, Principal Secretaries, and senior officials from across the country via video conferencing.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that DILRMP 3.0 is a decisive step toward improving Ease of Living for rural citizens, farmers, and property owners. He underscored that land in India is deeply tied to emotional and familial identities, making accurate and accessible documentation vital.

“Land is not just a piece of soil; it is the pride of our farmers, the blessing of our ancestors, and the identity of future generations,” said the Union Minister.

The Minister pointed out that the earlier phases of DILRMP successfully digitized 99.90% of Records of Rights (RoRs) and 97% of cadastral maps, alongside computerizing 99% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs). He noted that DILRMP 3.0 now raises the bar by moving from isolated digitization to full system integration, ensuring farmers can secure institutional credit easily and citizens are spared repeated visits to government offices.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister of State for Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, highlighted that DILRMP 3.0 will resolve legacy challenges by focusing on spatial accuracy, georeferenced maps, and seamless interoperability across departments.

Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Shri Narendra Bhooshan, delivered the welcome address and set the context for the guidelines, noting that DILRMP 3.0 marks a shift toward building an integrated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for land administration. Joint Secretary (LR), Shri Parikipandla Narahari, gave a comprehensive presentation detailing the technical architecture and scheme components.

Key Highlights of DILRMP 3.0

GIS-enabled ‘Land Stack’: Land Stack, an integrated digital framework would bring together different layers of land-related information such as georeferenced cadastral maps, Records of Rights, property registrations, and relevant court matters through GIS based digital interfaces. It will enable different land-related systems to be connected and accessed in an interoperable manner, while allowing each State to develop its own Land Stack by integrating its various land-related datasets and systems through APIs. These State-level Land Stacks would, in turn, form the building blocks of a National Land Stack, which would be developed in a federated manner, enabling seamless interoperability and exchange of information across States while retaining the respective ownership and control of data with the concerned authorities.

Universal Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN): Assigns a 14-digit unique identifier to every land parcel in the country to establish unambiguous property identities and eliminate fraud.

Registration Seva Kendras (RSKs): High-footfall 75 Sub-Registrar Offices will be modernized into citizen-friendly service centers with digital queue management and improved amenities, drawing inspiration from Passport Seva Kendras.

Scanning of Legacy Records: Historical land and property registration records will be systematically scanned and digitally archived to protect inheritance rights and curb ancestral land disputes.

Registration Repository: A secure digital framework of registered deeds and encumbrance information to enable ownership verification, transaction history and property due diligence.

Paperless Revenue Courts: Modernizes the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS) by linking it directly with land records to cut case pendency and expedite mutation settlements.

Urban Land Mapping (NAKSHA): Accelerates the NAKSHA pilot project to create accurate, GIS-based urban land records and issue Urban Property Cards (UrPro Cards).

Implementation and Monitoring

DILRMP 3.0 will be implemented across all States and Union Territories with 100% central funding under a phased, performance-linked mechanism managed through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Progress will be monitored in real time via an upgraded DILRMP-MIS dashboard overseen by the Project Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee (PS&MC). The event concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by the Director, DoLR.

(Release ID: 2308966)

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan officially launched the Operational Guidelines for the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0, introducing a GIS-based integrated framework known as the 'Land Stack' to enhance land record management across India.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Scheme Name**: Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0  
- **Funding**: Central Sector Scheme outlay of ₹565.50 Crore for the period 2026–2031  
- **Core Initiative**: Establishment of an integrated, GIS-based 'Land Stack' that consolidates georeferenced cadastral maps, Records of Rights (RoRs), property registrations, and court matters  
- **Service Centers**: Conversion of 75 Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) into modern 'Registration Seva Kendras' (RSKs) modeled after Passport Seva Kendras, featuring digital queue management and improved amenities  
- **Universal Identifier**: Introduction of a 14-digit Universal Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) for every land parcel to establish unambiguous property identities and prevent fraud  
- **Legacy Record Digitization**: Systematic scanning and digital archiving of historical land and property registration records to protect inheritance rights and resolve ancestral land disputes  
- **Registration Repository**: Creation of a secure digital framework for registered deeds and encumbrance information to facilitate ownership verification and due diligence  
- **Revenue Courts**: Modernization of the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS) by direct linkage with land records to reduce case pendency and expedite mutation settlements  
- **Urban Land Mapping**: Acceleration of the NAKSHA pilot project to produce accurate, GIS-based urban land records and issue Urban Property Cards (UrPro Cards)  
- **Implementation Scope**: Nationwide rollout across all States and Union Territories with 100% central funding under a phased, performance-linked mechanism managed through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS)  
- **Monitoring**: Real-time progress tracking via an upgraded DILRMP-MIS dashboard overseen by the Project Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee (PS&MC)

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah meets His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah meets His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi

India cherishes its bond with the Aga Khan Development Network, tied by a shared commitment to human development

Our discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in social development, irrigation, cooperatives, natural farming—including millets—and solar energy

Reaffirmed our shared commitment to advancing these partnerships for sustainable development and the greater good of humanity

10 SEP 2026 9:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah meets His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi today.

In his post on X platform, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said “Pleased to meet His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi. India cherishes its bond with the Aga Khan Development Network, tied by a shared commitment to human development. Our discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in social development, irrigation, cooperatives, natural farming—including millets—and solar energy. Reaffirmed our shared commitment to advancing these partnerships for sustainable development and the greater good of humanity.”

Pleased to meet His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi.

India cherishes its bond with the Aga Khan Development Network, tied by a shared commitment to human development.

Our discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in social development, irrigation, cooperatives, natural farming—including millets—and solar energy.

Reaffirmed our shared commitment to advancing these partnerships for sustainable development and the greater good of humanity.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah met Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi on 10 September 2026 to discuss strengthening cooperation between India and the Aga Khan Development Network in social development, irrigation, cooperatives, natural farming (including millets), and solar energy.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Meeting Details**: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah met His Highness Prince Rahim Aga Khan V in New Delhi.  
- **Date & Time**: 10 September 2026, 9:54 PM (PIB Delhi); announcement also posted on X (Twitter) on the same date.

- **Shared Commitment**: Reaffirmed dedication to advancing these partnerships for sustainable development and the greater good of humanity.

headline: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA
fullText:
Ministry of Power

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA

11 SEP 2026 8:41AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal will participate in the G20 Energy Ministerial Meeting to be held in the Houston, United States of America from 14–16 September 2026. The meeting, hosted under the U.S. G20 Presidency, will bring together Energy Ministers and senior representatives from G20 members to deliberate on key issues concerning global energy security, affordability, infrastructure development and resilient energy supply chains.

The Minister will participate in ministerial sessions under three key pillars - “Energy Security and Affordable Baseload,” “Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency,” and “Critical Minerals & Resilient Supply Chains.” The discussions will focus on strengthening energy security and affordability, facilitating timely development of energy infrastructure through efficient regulatory frameworks, and building secure, resilient and diversified critical-mineral supply chains.

During the meeting, Shri Manohar Lal will seek to highlight India’s approach towards building a resilient and future-ready energy system capable of meeting its rapidly growing energy needs while sharing India’s experience in enhancing permitting and regulatory efficiency through institutional and policy reforms as well as highlighting India’s focus on diversification, circularity, and strengthening the entire value chain of critical minerals.

The Minister’s participation will reaffirm India’s commitment to constructive international engagement and collective action in addressing evolving global energy challenges. India will continue to advocate pragmatic, inclusive and technology-neutral approaches that respect diverse national circumstances and advance secure, affordable, reliable, resilient and sustainable energy systems for all.

(Release ID: 2308993)
